questions.question: What do the white zig-zag lines beside a pedestrian crossing mean?
options: You must not park or overtake there
You may park for five minutes
You must speed up past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking and overtaking within crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: When may you enter a yellow criss-cross box junction to go straight ahead?
options: Whenever the traffic lights are green
Only when your exit road is clear
When the car ahead is still moving slowly
At any time if you signal
questions.explain: Rule 174: You must not enter a box junction unless your exit is clear.

questions.question: At speeds up to 30 mph. How much side space should you leave when overtaking a cyclist?
questions.explain: Rule 163: To leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists up to 30 mph.

questions.question: What minimum gap should you leave behind the car in front on a dry road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 sets at least a two-second gap in dry conditions.

questions.question: When should you give a signal before turning or changing lanes?
options: In good time before you make the move
Only when another car is behind you
Only at night or in rain
questions.explain: Rule 103: To give clear signals in good time.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car. In a built-up area with street lights, unless signed otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 30 mph as the standard built-up area limit for cars.

questions.question: What do red and amber lights showing together mean?
options: Also means stop; do not pass until green shows
questions.explain: Rule 175: Red and amber also means stop; you must wait for green.

questions.question: What do double broken white lines across the end of your road mean?
options: You have priority over cross traffic
Give way to traffic on the road you are joining
Stop for five seconds even if clear
questions.explain: Rule 172: Double broken lines mean give way to traffic on the main road.

questions.question: You are turning into a side road and a pedestrian is waiting to cross it. What should you do?
options: Sound your horn to warn them
Give way and let them cross
Speed up to clear the turn
Wave them to stay on the kerb
questions.explain: Rule H2: You should give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting. To cross a road into which or from which you are turning.

questions.question: Where should you position your car before turning left into a side road?
options: Well over to the left kerb
questions.explain: Rule 182: To keep well to the left before turning left.

questions.question: What must you check before changing lanes?
questions.explain: Rule 133: You must check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which side of the road should you normally drive on in the UK?
questions.explain: Rule 160: You should keep to the left unless overtaking or turning right.

questions.question: At a UK roundabout, which traffic must you give way to?
options: Traffic approaching from your immediate right
questions.explain: Rule 185: To give way to traffic approaching from your right.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when turning left at a roundabout?
questions.explain: Rule 186: Signalling left on approach when taking the first exit.

questions.question: When going straight ahead at a roundabout, when should you signal left?
options: Just after you pass the exit before the one you want
After you have left the roundabout
questions.explain: Rule 186: To signal left after passing the exit before yours.

questions.question: In Great Britain, which way must you drive around a roundabout?
options: Either way if no cars are there
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require going clockwise around UK roundabouts.

questions.question: What is the painted box with a bicycle symbol ahead of cars at traffic lights?
options: An advanced stop line (ASL) box for cyclists
questions.explain: Rule 178: Advanced stop lines give cyclists space at the front of the queue.

questions.question: What does a steady red traffic light mean?
options: Stop behind the white stop line
questions.explain: Rule 175: Red means stop and wait behind the stop line.

questions.question: What must you wait for before turning right across oncoming traffic?
options: A safe gap so oncoming cars do not slow
questions.explain: Rule 180: Wait until there is a safe gap before turning right.

questions.question: How should you drive around a multi-lane roundabout?
options: Keep inside your marked lane until you are ready to leave
Cut straight across the painted lines
Straddle two lanes so nobody passes
Always drift to the outer edge on bends
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 instructs drivers to stay in their lane around multi-lane roundabouts.

questions.question: Why are stop signs placed at certain junctions instead of Give Way signs?
options: Because the view of the main road is poor
questions.explain: Rule 171: stop signs are used where sightlines are restricted. So drivers must stop and look carefully.

questions.question: If road arrows and signs show a different lane plan than normal. What should you follow?
options: Follow the road markings and approach signs
Always stay in the right lane
questions.explain: Rule 186: tells drivers to follow painted lane arrows and approach signs when marked.

questions.question: When driving past a school in a 30 mph street, what is the safest approach?
options: Drop your speed well below 30 mph, around 20 mph
questions.explain: Rule 208: Lower speed gives you much shorter stopping distance if a child steps out.

questions.question: As you approach a green light that has been green for a long time. What should you expect?
options: It may change to amber soon, so be ready to brake
questions.explain: Rule 175: Expect stale green lights to change so you can stop smoothly on amber.

questions.question: Why should you not wave a pedestrian across at a zebra crossing?
options: Another vehicle could be approaching from the other way
It is illegal to raise a hand
questions.explain: Rule 195 warns against waving pedestrians across because other drivers may not stop.

questions.question: After stopping at the white line, you still cannot see clearly. What should you do?
options: Creep forward slowly until you can see
questions.explain: Rule 171: Stop at the line first. Then edge forward slowly to get a clear view before pulling out.

questions.question: When going straight ahead at a normal two-lane roundabout with no special arrows. Which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 recommends the left-hand lane for straight ahead unless signs direct otherwise.

questions.question: At what times of day should you still watch for children near a school?
options: Any time, including clubs, lunchtimes, and weekends
questions.explain: Rule 208: Schools and playgrounds are used outside normal bell times too.

questions.question: Before braking for an amber light, what should you check?
questions.explain: Rule 175: Check your mirror to judge whether. A vehicle close behind makes hard braking unsafe.

questions.question: When may you move off after stopping at a zebra crossing?
options: As soon as they reach the middle
Once they have crossed safely clear of your path
Before they step off the stripes
While they are still in front of your lane
questions.explain: Rule 195: Wait until pedestrians have safely cleared the crossing before moving off.

questions.question: Why is overtaking banned inside crossing zig-zag lines?
options: The overtaken car can hide a pedestrian stepping onto the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 protects pedestrians whose view of approaching cars is blocked.

questions.question: When are you allowed to stop inside a yellow box junction?
options: When turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic to clear
When queuing to go straight ahead
questions.explain: Rule 174: allows stopping in the box only. When turning right and blocked by oncoming cars.

questions.question: What should you do if there is not enough. Room to pass a cyclist with 1.5 metres to spare?
options: Wait behind the cyclist until it is safe to pass wide
Flash your headlights until they mount the pavement
questions.explain: Rule 163: To wait behind if you cannot leave enough room to overtake safely.

questions.question: Why is a fixed two-car-length gap unsafe at 70 mph?
options: Stopping distance grows sharply at high speed
questions.explain: Rule 126: uses time rather than car lengths because stopping distance rises with speed.

questions.question: If you signal early, does that give you the right to pull out?
options: Yes, other drivers must stop for you
No, you must still wait until it is safe
Yes, if you signal for three seconds
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds drivers that signals show intent and never give priority.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car on a single-lane-each-way rural road?
questions.explain: Rule 124: sets 60 mph for cars on single rural roads without lower signs.

questions.question: A driver behind beeps as soon as red and amber show. What should you do?
options: Move across on red and amber
Wait behind the line until green and check it is safe
questions.explain: Rule 175: Never let another driver pressure you into crossing before green.

questions.question: When must you stop completely behind a solid. White line with a red octagonal stop sign?
options: Every time, even if the road looks clear
questions.explain: Rule 171: and Rule 172 require a full stop at a stop sign and line.

questions.question: Does Rule H2 apply when you turn out of a. Side road as well as when you turn into one?
options: Yes, both turning into and out of a road
questions.explain: Rule H2 covers pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross. A road you are turning into or out of.

questions.question: Before moving close to the left kerb for a left turn, what should you check?
options: Your nearside mirror and blind spot for cyclists
questions.explain: Rule 182 warns to watch out for cyclists coming up on your left.

questions.question: In slow queuing traffic, when should you change lanes?
options: Whenever a tiny gap opens for a moment
Only when it is safe and you will not block others
As fast as possible before the queue stops
Without signalling so others do not speed up
questions.explain: Rule 133: Not weaving between lanes or cutting across other drivers.

questions.question: What if the first exit is straight ahead and there is no left turn?
options: Treat it as straight ahead and do not signal on approach unless signs show left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 matches your signal to the road layout and signs.

questions.question: After you have entered the exit road from a roundabout, what should you do?
options: Check your left signal has cancelled
Leave the left signal on for 300 metres
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require cancelling your signal once clear.

questions.question: What should you do if temporary roadworks traffic. Lights are stuck on red for a long time?
options: Wait and check if they are faulty before moving only with extreme care
questions.explain: Rule 176: Never assume a red light is broken quickly. Only proceed with extreme caution if clearly failed.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, three cars arrive at once and nobody has clear priority. What should you do?
options: Make eye contact, proceed slowly, and give way if unsure
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and courtesy advice help resolve deadlocks safely.

questions.question: On a spiral roundabout, how do the lane markings guide you?
options: They gradually lead you outward toward your exit
They mean you must stop on the island
questions.explain: Rule 186: Following lane markings that guide you cleanly out to your exit.

questions.question: Can large lorries sometimes touch the edge of a painted mini-roundabout circle?
options: Yes, long vehicles may need to, but cars must drive around it clockwise
Only cars may drive over it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 note cars must pass around the circle clockwise.

questions.question: In heavy rain, why do blind-spot checks matter even more before changing lanes?
options: Spray reduces what you can see in side mirrors
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and wet-weather advice warn that spray hides vehicles in mirrors.

questions.question: A lorry on the roundabout is taking the next exit. Blocking your view of the lane behind it. What should you do?
options: Wait until the lorry clears so you can see any hidden vehicles behind it
questions.explain: Rule 185: Not to enter when a large vehicle hides traffic to your right.

questions.question: At a tiny mini-roundabout with little space, should you still signal your turn?
options: Yes, signal clearly in good time before entering
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and 188 still require clear approach signals at mini-roundabouts.
